page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. The first paragraph's line "senatorium est ordinem" is printed as "fenatorium eft ordinem"; the "f" for long s is normalised to s. The original line 1 of XIII has "fuam" and "ingenij" as printed. Lines in XVII read "nauaret:cum" with colon as printed. The word "tectaq;" is printed "tectaq;" with a semicolon-q abbreviation. Some words in the italic-like type of the section numerals (XIII–XVII) are set in roman in the printing and are transcribed as shown. The sentence "XVII ... cum de literis literatisq;" is printed as "teris literatisq;" with the first word partly cut by the gutter; reading is conjectural. Words marked [?] were not clearly legible: none marked, but the gutter-side word "teris" should be checked against the scan.
